events.title: Bush by 21
events.text: George W. Bush carried Kansas by 20.8 points.

events.title: Brownback re-elected
events.text: Sam Brownback won a second full Senate term with 69.1 percent.

events.title: Sebelius re-elected
events.text: Democrat Kathleen Sebelius won a second term as governor with 57.9 percent.

events.title: The margin narrows
events.text: John McCain carried Kansas by 15 points, the closest presidential race of the decade.

events.title: “A real live experiment”
events.text: On 19 June Governor Brownback said of his income-tax cuts: “We'll have a real live experiment.”

events.title: Moderates ousted
events.text: In the August primary, conservatives defeated most moderate Republican state senators, including Senate President Steve Morris of Hugoton.

events.title: Roberts holds on
events.text: Pat Roberts beat the independent Greg Orman, 53.1 to 42.5 percent, after the Democratic nominee withdrew.

events.title: Marshall to Congress
events.text: Roger Marshall, an obstetrician from Great Bend, was elected to the U.S. House from the 1st District.

events.title: Moderates return
events.text: In the August primary, moderate Republicans won eight state Senate races, ousting six incumbents.

events.title: Tax cuts repealed
events.text: On 6 June the Legislature overrode Brownback's veto, raising about $1.2 billion over two years.

events.title: Governor Kelly
events.text: Democrat Laura Kelly beat Kris Kobach, 48.0 to 43.0 percent.

events.title: Bollier switches
events.text: In December state Senator Barbara Bollier, of Mission Hills, left the Republican Party for the Democrats.

events.title: A Methodist split
events.text: In May, United Methodists opposed to the church's ban on LGBTQ clergy met at the Church of the Resurrection in Leawood.

events.title: Johnson County turns
events.text: Joe Biden carried Johnson County by 8.2 points; Trump had won it by 2.6 in 2016.

events.title: Marshall elected
events.text: Marshall beat Bollier for the Senate, 53.2 to 41.8 percent; Bollier carried Johnson County.

events.title: Electoral objections
events.text: On 6 January Marshall voted to sustain objections to Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes.

events.title: Bob Dole dies
events.text: Bob Dole, senator for Kansas from 1969 to 1996, died on 5 December.

events.title: Amendment fails
events.text: On 2 August Kansans rejected an amendment on abortion, 59.2 to 40.8 percent.

events.title: Split decision
events.text: In November Kansans re-elected Governor Kelly by 2.2 points and Senator Moran by 23; the Libertarian David Graham won 3 percent.

events.title: Trump by 16
events.text: Donald Trump carried Kansas by 16.1 points; Kamala Harris carried Johnson County by 8.4.

events.title: Sorghum stalls
events.text: From April China's tariffs halted its purchases of U.S. sorghum, much of it grown in Kansas.

events.title: Budget law passes
events.text: On 1 July the Senate passed the tax-and-spending law, 51 to 50; Marshall had promoted it.

events.title: Boeing buys Spirit
events.text: On 8 December Boeing completed its purchase of Spirit AeroSystems, Wichita's largest employer.

events.title: Marshall files
events.text: On 22 January Marshall filed for re-election, with President Trump's endorsement.

events.title: Hamilton explores
events.text: In February Adam Hamilton formed a committee to explore an independent run.

events.title: Libertarians in Wichita
events.text: On 25 April the Libertarian state convention in Wichita nominated David C. Graham.

events.title: Hamilton runs
events.text: On 30 April Hamilton entered the race as “an independent-minded Democrat.”

events.title: Livestock group holds back
events.text: On 2 July the Kansas Livestock Association's PAC declined to endorse Marshall.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 4 August Marshall won 79.9 percent and Hamilton 34.6 percent of an eleven-way Democratic race.

events.title: Kassebaum dies
events.text: Nancy Landon Kassebaum, the first woman to represent Kansas in the Senate, died on 21 August.

events.title: Farm Bureau backs Marshall
events.text: On 26 August the Kansas Farm Bureau endorsed Marshall.

events.title: Medical-debt report
events.text: In September the New York Times reported that Marshall's former practice had sued more than 700 patients.

events.title: Graves backs Hamilton
events.text: On 9 September former Republican Governor Bill Graves endorsed Hamilton.

events.title: State Fair debate
events.text: On 12 September Marshall and Hamilton debated at the Kansas State Fair in Hutchinson.

events.title: Vance in Olathe
events.text: On 14 September Vice President JD Vance rallied for Marshall in Olathe.

events.title: Hayden backs Hamilton
events.text: On 2 October former Republican Governor Mike Hayden endorsed Hamilton.

events.title: A toss-up
events.text: On 6 October the Cook Political Report rated the race a toss-up; Sabato's Crystal Ball followed on 14 October.

events.title: Brownback backs Marshall
events.text: On 13 October former Governor Sam Brownback endorsed Marshall.

events.title: Ballots go out
events.text: On 14 October mail ballots went out and advance voting could begin.

events.title: Trump in Park City
events.text: On 19 October President Trump held a rally for Marshall in Park City, near Wichita.

events.title: TV debate
events.text: Nexstar set a televised debate between Marshall and Hamilton for 21 October, from Kansas City; Graham was not invited.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Kansans choose between Graham, Hamilton and Marshall.

chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; FEC certified results). It is a simplification: Kansas elects its senator in its own race, and Kansans often split their tickets (in 2022 they re-elected a Democratic governor by two points and a Republican senator by twenty-three), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on Kansas, so outer states are cut at the edge.
